title: 四级篇章听力：天气笔记、项目估时与棋社
instruction: 听完整一节3篇短文及各段后读出的问题，依次选择最佳答案。音频中材料和问题各读一遍，卷面只印四个选项。本原创使用节内编号1—10，各段对应1—3、4—6、7—10题。播放器可回听，正式单次听辨条件未强制。
audio_introduction: Section C. You will hear three passages. After each, you will hear questions. Each recording and each question will be spoken only once. Choose the best answer from A, B, C and D.
source_form_notice: 四级形式参照2024年12月第一套转载Section C：3段、3/3/4共10回应、每题四选；原创采用节内编号，问题只在录音与作者区。全部自有虚构内容及本机合成试听，非原考试原声；未独立教研/听辨/学生难度或产品等值验证。

turns.speaker: R
turns.text: For nearly thirty years, retired shopkeeper Nora Bell wrote down the weather outside her kitchen window every morning. Her notebooks contain no complicated measurements. She noted whether the road was wet, which hills she could see, and when the apple tree began to flower. After she moved to a smaller home, her grandson suggested throwing the notebooks away. Nora almost agreed, since the information was never intended for anyone else. A local history group persuaded her to keep them. Its members were studying changes in everyday life in the village and found the notes useful alongside photographs and newspaper reports. They did not treat a wet road as a precise measure of rainfall. Instead, the notes sometimes helped explain why an outdoor event was moved or why a particular journey took longer than expected. The group has copied the notebooks and returned the originals to Nora. Some dates are difficult to read, and a few pages are missing, so the collection cannot provide a complete daily record. Even so, it offers details that more formal records often leave out. Nora now writes a sentence about what she did as well as what she saw. She says the group's interest has reminded her that an ordinary day can become interesting when someone looks back at it years later.

questions.spoken_question: Why did Nora originally keep the notebooks?
options: To make observations for her own use.
To supply exact rainfall data to a weather station.
To prepare a book for a local newspaper.
To compare different villages for a research project.
questions.rationale: A：never intended for anyone else，个人日记；B未精密测量；C未为报纸成书；D无跨村研究原计划。

questions.spoken_question: How did the history group use Nora's notes?
options: As a replacement for all photographs of the village.
As proof that her weather measurements were exact.
As a complete record with no missing information.
As supporting details for understanding local events.
questions.rationale: D：结合照片/报纸解释活动改期、旅程用时；A alongside非替代；B不把wet road当降雨量；C有缺页/不清日期。

questions.spoken_question: What change has Nora made to her writing?
options: She now records the weather only once a month.
She adds something about her own daily activities.
She writes only about events reported in newspapers.
She sends all her original notebooks to the history group.
questions.rationale: B：现在加what she did；A未降频；C仍个人观察；D原件归还她，未移交全部原本。

turns.speaker: R
turns.text: When a student group was asked to produce a short documentary, its members quickly divided the work. One would arrange interviews, another would film, and a third would edit the material. Each person estimated how long their own part would take. Added together, the estimates seemed to leave plenty of time before the deadline. The difficulty was that the tasks could not all happen independently. The editor could not begin with the main interviews until the filming was finished, and the filming depended on people agreeing to be interviewed. One cancellation therefore affected much more than a single afternoon. After their first delay, the students drew a simple chart showing which activities had to come before others. They also marked smaller jobs, such as choosing background music, that could be done while they waited for an interview. The chart did not make interviewees easier to contact, and it could not prevent equipment problems. It did, however, help the students see where a delay would matter most. They finished the film a day before the deadline, after removing a planned extra interview. In their final report, the group said its original mistake was treating a list of individual working hours as if it were a timetable. For its next project, it would discuss the order of tasks before promising a completion date.

questions.spoken_question: What was the main weakness in the students' original plan?
options: They gave every member exactly the same job.
They allowed too much time for filming each interview.
They overlooked how some tasks depended on others.
They refused to estimate the hours needed for editing.
questions.rationale: C：个人时数相加忽略先后依赖；A有明确分工；B未称拍摄估时过多；D已经估时，非拒估。

questions.spoken_question: What did the chart help the group do?
options: Identify the delays that would have the greatest effect.
Guarantee that every interview would take place on time.
Avoid the need to contact people for interviews.
Finish all filming and editing simultaneously.
questions.rationale: A：where delay matter most；B不能保证约人；C约人仍需；D主要编辑仍依赖拍完，不能同时全做。

questions.spoken_question: What did the students decide to do on their next project?
options: Add an extra interview at the last minute.
Let only the editor choose the completion date.
Ignore smaller jobs until all interviews are finished.
Discuss the sequence of tasks before setting a deadline.
questions.rationale: D：末句先讨论order再承诺完成日；A本次删去加访谈不是新计划；B团队讨论非编辑独定；C小任务可等候时做。

turns.speaker: R
turns.text: The Thursday chess club at a community center was originally so quiet that visitors were sometimes unsure whether they were allowed to enter. Experienced players would begin a game immediately, while newcomers watched from a distance. The coordinator, Ben, noticed that several first-time visitors left without asking to play. He decided to introduce a short welcome session before the games. At first, he tried explaining all the rules to the whole room. Regular members became impatient, and beginners found there was too much to remember. Ben then changed the arrangement. Experienced volunteers now sit at a separate table for the first fifteen minutes, where newcomers can try a few moves and ask questions. Regular games continue elsewhere in the room. There is no requirement to attend the welcome table, and visitors who already know the game can join a match straight away. The club also lends small chess sets for use at home, although borrowers must return them before taking another. Ben does not measure the change simply by counting how many people walk through the door. He is more interested in how many first-time visitors return. He says the purpose of the new arrangement is not to turn every visitor into a competition player. It is to make the club a place where people feel comfortable admitting that they are still learning.

questions.spoken_question: What did Ben notice about some first-time visitors?
options: They left without asking to join a game.
They borrowed sets but never returned them.
They interrupted experienced players with too many questions.
questions.rationale: B：若干新客未问就走；A没有竞技要求；C借棋后续措施，未欠还；D反而保持距离，非频繁打断。

questions.spoken_question: Why did Ben stop explaining all the rules to the whole room?
options: The room was too small for all club members.
No experienced players were willing to volunteer.
The center had prohibited any spoken instructions.
The approach frustrated regulars and overwhelmed beginners.
questions.rationale: D：熟手不耐烦/新手记不住；A空间原因未提；B有志愿者；C无禁讲规则。

questions.spoken_question: What can visitors who already know chess do?
options: Join a game without attending the welcome table.
Borrow a second set before returning the first.
Require the regular games to stop for fifteen minutes.
Attend a competition before entering the club.
questions.rationale: A：already know straightaway；B必须先还；C主区照常；D未设赛资格门槛。

questions.spoken_question: What does Ben regard as a useful sign that the change is working?
options: More chess sets being stored at the center.
More first-time visitors coming back to the club.
More rules being explained before every game.
questions.rationale: C：关心首访者返场；A不以竞技转化为目标；B库存非效果；D已放弃全员讲所有规则。
